title: Starting — Air Starter Motor Replacement and Extended Duty Cycle Release
abstract: Replacement of both air starter motors by the revised clutch variant and release of the extended five-attempt duty cycle, aimed at operators using high altitude airfields in hot conditions.

sections.planning_reason: Operators flying into airfields above six thousand feet in summer temperatures exceed the published duty cycle almost every day, because a hot start abort followed by a cooling period and a second attempt uses two of the three permitted cycles before the aircraft has moved. The starter removal rate at three such operators has reached one per four thousand cycles against a fleet average of one per fourteen thousand, and returned units show clutch spragging damage consistent with re-engagement above the permitted residual speed.
sections.description: The bulletin replaces both starters with the revised clutch variant, changes the inlet nozzle and clamp to suit the higher flow, and re-issues the cranking shroud with the larger inspection aperture. The extended duty cycle is released only when both engines carry the new starter.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Open the fan cowl and support it. Do the removal task AMM-C-80-10-11-000-022-A for the starter. Remove the nozzle assembly HOL790179-18 and the clamp PE187919-09 at the starter air inlet. Install the new nozzle assembly and the wider clamp and torque the bolts EN290030-3C. Install the revised starter and connect the air inlet duct. Install the cranking shroud ASDE222426-98 with the larger inspection aperture and check that the clutch witness mark can be read through it. Install the start valve clamp ZE172964-77. Do the installation task AMM-C-80-10-11-400-022-A and then a dry motoring run with the residual speed recorded. Repeat on the other engine. Update the aircraft operating limitations with the extended duty cycle only when both engines are at the new standard. Close up and record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to CIRRANE-13 aircraft with PYR-1524G or PYR-1525G engines. The extended five-attempt duty cycle may only be used when both engines carry the revised starter, and the limitation section of the flight crew operating manual states this explicitly. Aircraft from MSN C00680 onward are already at the standard.
sections.material_note: Kit K8010-2001-01 is supplied per engine and contains the starter, the nozzle assembly, the clamp, the shroud and the fastener set. Lead time is twenty weeks. Removed starters are returned to the supplier under the exchange agreement and attract a credit.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next starter replacement for any reason, or within forty-eight months of the date of this Service Bulletin for operators using airfields above six thousand feet.
